chief_complaint: desire for breast reconstruction after breast cancer surgery
hpi_details: A 65-year-old man seeks reconstruction after mastectomy for breast cancer and wants to discuss timing and reconstructive options in coordination with his oncology team.
ideas: thinks it might be related to breast_reconstruction
concerns: worried about potential complications and long term recovery
expectations: wants complete diagnostic evaluation and treatment plan

core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Post-Mastectomy Reconstruction is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.

Standard management emphasizes Plan for Post-Mastectomy Reconstruction: Discuss reconstruction options: tissue expander/implants vs DIEP flap, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: desire for breast reconstruction after breast cancer surgery
Key HPI features: A 65-year-old man seeks reconstruction after mastectomy for breast cancer and needs coordinated oncologic and surgical planning.
Objective/Exam findings: Focused physical exam and vital signs check. Tailored diagnostics for Post-Mastectomy Reconstruction.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Post-Mastectomy Reconstruction.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Soft tissue infection without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Proceeding without coordinating with oncology or optimizing factors that increase reconstructive risk.
management_principles: Plan for Post-Mastectomy Reconstruction: Discuss reconstruction options: tissue expander/implants vs DIEP flap
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

teaching.one_liner: Plastic and reconstructive surgical case presenting with desire for breast reconstruction after breast cancer surgery.
differentials: Recurrent breast cancer requiring oncologic workup before reconstruction
Chest wall radiation fibrosis limiting reconstructive options
Implant-related complication in a prior reconstruction
red_flags: New chest-wall mass, persistent wound breakdown, fever, or drainage requiring prompt assessment for recurrence or infection
Active smoking, uncontrolled diabetes, vascular disease, or planned radiation requiring risk optimization and multidisciplinary timing

must_ask.say: When did you have your mastectomy, and was it on one side or both?
Did you have radiation or chemotherapy as part of your treatment?
Have you thought about whether you'd prefer implants or using your own tissue?
Do you smoke, and do you have diabetes or any circulation problems?
How has the mastectomy affected you emotionally, and what worries you most about reconstruction?
